source.title: Diffusion Beats Autoregressive in Data-Constrained Settings
source.authors: Mihir Prabhudesai; Meng-Ning Wu; A. Zadeh; Katerina Fragkiadaki; Deepak Pathak

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study fits and evaluates data-constrained scaling laws using a modified method and repeated-data experiments, rather than reproducing the original single-epoch scaling-law setup.
record.gate_note: The study reports fitted scaling-law metrics, validation-loss behavior under repeated training, and a critical-compute frontier. The downstream benchmark tables compare selected models, but do not establish a predictable relationship between downstream performance and scale or pretraining loss. Results attributed to prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits the Muennighoff data-constrained (repeated-data) power-law loss law to about 200 of its own AR and masked-diffusion LM runs. It reports fit quality, fitted reuse parameters and loss curves under repetition. This is a new setting (diffusion LMs, many epochs) with results on V1, V5 (repeated data is a named V5 regime) and V7 (curves bending with repetition; parameters depending on model family).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that masked diffusion LMs exploit repeated data far better than AR (R_D* ≈500 vs ≈31) and beat AR in validation loss beyond a critical compute that scales as U^2.174. Their takeaway: use AR when compute-constrained, diffusion when data-constrained. Downstream gains are shown only for selected best models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses repeated-data training and a data-constrained scaling-law formulation with effective data and parameter quantities, rather than reproducing the original single-epoch scaling-law procedure. It compares masked diffusion and AR models trained on C4.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ by model family and training repetition: AR shows overfitting at high epoch counts, whereas diffusion shows no signs of overfitting in the explored budget. The reported effective data-reuse half-life also differs sharply between the families.

fits_no_version.finding: The compute at which diffusion matches AR loss scales as a power law in unique tokens (Ccrit ∝ U^2.174), and empirical crossover points align with the fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The diffusion-vs-AR crossover compute grows as a power of unique dataset size in data-constrained LM pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: At 100M unique tokens, diffusion's best loss (3.55) beats AR's (3.71), and downstream accuracy is higher for the selected best diffusion model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Masked diffusion LMs are more sample-efficient than AR LMs under data repetition.

record.problems: The authors state that their scaling laws are fitted over a limited range of unique data sizes. The text provides no error bars or confidence intervals for the reported scaling-law fits. Table 1 and its accompanying prose give inconsistent RD* values for both model families. Some large-compute repeated-data curves are extrapolated rather than validated against actual larger runs.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for downstream benchmark accuracies in Tables 2-4: these compare selected models but do not test predictable downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss. No additional per-compute frontier points from Figure 6 are separately tabulated in the text.

untested.parts: No pure single-epoch law across several orders of magnitude of compute is reported separately; fits use effective N' and D'.
Figure 5 extrapolates to 1e19–1e20 FLOPs, but no larger run is checked against the prediction. The 500M-token, 2.3B diffusion run reports no loss compared with a prediction.
Not tested; single-epoch compute-optimal sizes are taken from prior laws.
Width and depth are scaled together; shape is not varied at fixed N.
Only text and repeated data; no other modalities, fine-tuning or transfer.
Downstream results compare only selected best models (Tables 2–4), not performance as a function of scale or loss.
Fitting method, parameter counting and schedule are not varied.

missing.what: Decay rate of the value of repeated data: fitted curves match empirical points, and the decay rate is consistent across 1e19, 3e19 and 1e20 FLOPs for both families.
At a fixed 1e19 compute, AR validation-loss curves diverge (overfit) with more epochs while diffusion curves overlap.
Pareto frontier of loss vs FLOPs for 25M, 50M and 100M unique tokens: AR saturates and overfits beyond Chinchilla-optimal compute, while diffusion keeps improving.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'V5 not tested' is wrong: repeated data is an explicit V5 regime. Single-epoch losses quoted at the compute-optimal stars (10.65 vs 7.07) look implausibly high and may be mislabelled. The paper reports no error bars on the fits. R_D* values differ between table and prose. Extrapolated curves (Figure 5) are not validated against real larger runs, so they do not test V2.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the conventional single-epoch loss laws across parameters, unique tokens, and compute over several orders of magnitude. Its fitted law uses effective quantities to model repeated-data effects.
The study extrapolates fitted curves, but does not report a test of small-run loss fits against actual runs orders of magnitude larger.
It does not test how both compute-optimal parameter count and token count scale with compute, or compare their growth rates.
It does not vary depth, width, or architecture at a fixed parameter count to measure their effect on loss.
The experiments are language-model pretraining on text; other modalities, fine-tuning, and transfer are not tested.
The study evaluates selected models on downstream tasks but does not test predictable downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
The study does not systematically vary fitting choices or quantify disagreements between published exponents or compute-optimal allocations.

source_check.notes: Table 1 and Section 3.2 disagree on both families' reuse parameters. Figure 5 is extrapolated; its cross-family absolute losses are not directly comparable because the fitted entropy terms differ.

statements.correction: AR effective-resource repeated-data fit: initial R²=0.9439; second-step R²=0.7628. Unique-token budgets: 25M, 50M, 100M. Direct relevance: V5; V1's non-bottleneck condition untested.
statements.problem: The AR second-step R² and repeated-data setting are correct. This constrained effective-resource fit does not establish a limitation of V1 within its explicitly non-bottleneck regime.

statements.correction: Masked diffusion: no observed overfitting within the explored compute budget; training explored up to 800 epochs; 100M-token contour optimum at 500 epochs. Approximate agreement with fresh-data scaling through 100 epochs is extrapolated. These observations do not contradict V7.
statements.problem: The reported absence of diffusion overfitting and the extrapolation caveat are accurate. Treating them as evidence against V7 overstates their implication: V7 says curves can bend, not that every model must overfit.
